classification.difficultyReason: Read the quadrant of each point and find its acute reference angle. For Q and R the diagram marks the reference angle, but for P it gives the full 150°, so 30° must be derived. Then write signed (cos, sin) coordinates, which is slightly more than p34-q5.

content.prompt:
The points $P,Q,R$ are on the unit circle. $O$ is the origin.
Find the coordinates of $P,Q,R$.
Leave your answer in terms of $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the acute reference angle.

answer.worked:
On the unit circle, the coordinate magnitudes are $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the acute reference angle. Use the quadrant to determine their signs.

$P$ is in Q2, $Q$ is in Q3 and $R$ is in Q4.

$$\begin{align*}\theta_P&=180^{\circ}-150^{\circ}=30^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P&=(-\cos30^{\circ},\sin30^{\circ})\\Q&=(-\cos55^{\circ},-\sin55^{\circ})\\R&=(\cos70^{\circ},-\sin70^{\circ}).\end{align*}$$
